properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: md5@2.3.0 locked in yarn.lock and shipped in the bundle; no call site found in app/ source — presence-only entry. Changeable here by removing the dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry: node-forge@1.3.1 is resolved in yarn.lock (pulled transitively by react-native tooling) and ships in the JS bundle; it exposes RSA keygen/encrypt/sign plus TLS/CSR/PKCS#12 implementations. No direct node-forge import found in app/ code, but the bundle carries the library. Changeable here by pruning/upgrading the dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/curves@1.8.1 (transitive via Solana JS SDK) ships secp256k1 — available in the shipped library even though no direct app call site was found. Presence is what the inventory records; use is a separate question. Changeable only by upgrading the SDK.

components.name: Node.js tls sessions on default settings (at least Node.js 16)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry: @noble/curves resolved in yarn.lock (entry "@noble/curves@^1.4.2"), transitively pulled (e.g. via Solana packages using @noble/ed25519). The bundle ships Ed25519/ECDH curve implementations whether or not the app code calls them directly; the app's own Ed25519 goes through tweetnacl/@ton/crypto instead.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency AND actively installed: App.tsx:15 calls installSolana() to register this polyfill so @solana/web3.js Ed25519 (WebCrypto Ed25519) works under React Native. This is the Solana signing path used by the solana_proof in ConnectReplyBuilder.ts.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/curves@1.8.1 ships P-256; available in the shipped library, no direct app call site found in this tree (reachable via Solana/web3 dependencies). Changeable only by upgrading the SDK.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl@1.0.3 ships X25519 (box). The app calls tweetnacl directly for Ed25519 signing (see Ed25519 findings) and uses its XSalsa20-Poly1305 secretbox via @ton/crypto sealBox/openBox; no direct X25519/box call site found in app code — X25519 availability rides on tweetnacl. Changeable by migrating the library.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The wallet's Android secure-storage encrypter: AndroidKeyStore-generated AES-256 key (AES_KEY_SIZE_BITS = 256 at line 307, resolving the object's "key size unstated" note), AES/GCM/NoPadding, fresh IV per write, per-use device-credential/biometric authentication (setUserAuthenticationRequired(true), validity duration 0), strongbox deliberately off. Quantum-safe AE at CNSA 2.0's required key size; changeable here (the file is first-party code).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry: AES resolved in yarn.lock (transitive — e.g. via react-native-quick-crypto and other native crypto wrappers installed in App.tsx). The bundle ships AES implementations; the app's own first-party AES use is the AndroidKeyStore AES-256-GCM in KeyStoreModule.java (separate object, confirmed).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry: SHA-2-256 resolved via lockfile deps (notably @ton/crypto, whose sha256_sync the app calls directly for hash-then-sign in ConnectReplyBuilder.ts, signWalletRequest.ts and useCloudValue.ts). The live hash-then-sign uses are reported as separate Ed25519-signature findings.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry: BLAKE3 resolved transitively in yarn.lock. No direct BLK3 call site found in app code; the bundle ships the implementation.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/hashes@1.7.1 ships SHA-3; quantum-safe hash, available in the shipped library, no direct app call site found. Changeable by dependency upgrade only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl@1.0.3 ships XSalsa20-Poly1305 (secretbox/box). Live call sites exist through the @ton/crypto wrapper (sealBox/openBox in app/storage/secureStorage.ts and app/engine/hooks/cloud/useCloudValue.ts) — reported as separate findings. Symmetric AE: quantum-resistance adequate (256-bit key, Grover-only).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: node-forge@1.3.1 (X.509/PKI/TLS toolkit) locked in yarn.lock; shipped in the bundle, no app call site found in this tree (likely a transitive dev/runtime dep). Presence-only entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry: the md5 package resolved in the lockfile ships an MD5 implementation in the bundle. No first-party call site found in app code; retained because presence is what the dependency inventory records. MD5's collision weaknesses are irrelevant to its typical cache-key use but the asset is correctly inventoried as quantum-unsafe-adjacent weak hash.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory entry: @noble/hashes (1.7.1, per the "@noble/hashes@1.7.1, @noble/hashes@^1.3.1, @noble/hashes@^1.4.0" lock entry) provides SHA-2/SHA-3/BLAKE/RIPEMD implementations to the bundle — it also explains the SHA-3 and BLAKE3 dependency sightings in this inventory. Transitively consumed (via Solana/TON ecosystem packages).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/curves@1.8.1 is the elliptic-curve library shipping secp256k1/P-256 (transitive via the Solana JS SDK). No direct app call site found; availability follows the dependency. Changeable by upgrading/removing the SDK dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: node-forge@1.3.1 shipped in the bundle (X.509/TLS/RSA toolkit); no app call site found in this tree. Presence is what this entry records — the library's algorithms ship whether or not this application calls them.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Committed Android debug signing keystore (standard RN practice; well-known credentials androiddebugkey/android). Signs debug APK builds only — not release material, and not wallet key material. Changeable here in the trivial sense (regenerate); the entry's value is recording that the app's debug builds are signed by a publicly-known key, which is expected posture, not a secret leak.
